subject: Cognitive Science
title: Mental Simulation
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Mental Simulation.

hook.text: Before building a bridge, an engineer imagines it bending under weight. The bridge exists only in her mind.

buildup.text: Mental simulation lets us test plans, predict outcomes, and rehearse actions without real-world cost.

discovery.text: The brain uses the same circuits for simulating as for perceiving—imagination borrows from reality.

twist.text: But simulations inherit our biases. We imagine best cases, forget edge cases, and skip boring parts.

climax.text: Pre-mortem thinking fixes this: imagine the plan already failed and work backward to find why.

punchline.text: Run the movie in your mind before you press play.

quiz.question: What is a pre-mortem?
options: Imagining a plan has failed and analyzing why

details.summary: Mental simulation is the ability to run scenarios in your imagination, predicting how events might unfold by mentally rehearsing actions and outcomes. This capacity underpins planning, empathy, problem-solving, and counterfactual thinking throughout daily life.
details.whyItMatters: The ability to simulate futures in your mind before acting is one of humanity's most powerful cognitive abilities. It lets you learn from imagined experience.
takeaways: Mental simulation lets you rehearse actions before performing them
It supports planning, empathy, and counterfactual reasoning
Accuracy improves with expertise in the simulated domain

faq.question: How accurate are mental simulations?
faq.answer: Accuracy depends heavily on domain expertise. Expert chess players simulate many moves ahead accurately. Novices simulate poorly. Mental simulations are also biased by emotions, desires, and the availability heuristic. They are useful tools but not reliable crystal balls.

faq.question: Can mental simulation help with decision-making?
faq.answer: Yes. Premortem analysis asks you to imagine a project has already failed, then simulate why. This mental simulation surfaces risks you would otherwise overlook. Prospective hindsight, imagining looking back from the future, reliably improves planning quality.
